checkpoints.description: [1/3] Add ui_required to project config and enforce it in check --strict and publish, closing the publish bypass. [2/3] Add ui verify --json with stable finding codes. [3/3] Add a React/Vite ui init pilot that writes a conservative contract. Measure adoption and false positives before adding browser proof.

impact_assessment.why: The manager review approved closing the opt-in bypass, adding machine-readable output, and piloting one stack before any rendered/visual/a11y platform work.
impact_assessment.benefits: UI projects that opt in cannot publish or pass strict delivery without a contract and a closed UI task; CI can consume findings without scraping prose; one real stack gets a low-friction contract.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: ui_required adds a project config key and publish now refuses non-delivery-ready trees; dependency: none; concurrency: no new shared state; state: no ledger schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep ui_required opt-in, add migration-free defaults, test check/publish refusal, keep the JSON shape additive, and add no external dependency.

checkpoints.description: [milestone 1/3] Added ui_required enforcement: strict check and publish now refuse a missing .aikit/ui.json, and publish runs the delivery baseline before uploading. Added ADR-166, docs and tests. 392 unit tests at 7.47ms/test (10ms), 49 integration at 218.51ms/test (350ms); sync, knowledge, secrets, reachability, hygiene and dogfood clean. checklists: passed. Uncommitted.

[milestone 1/3] Verification found and fixed two enforcement holes: ui_required now validates the contract instead of only checking file existence, and plain check skips auto-push when the required UI contract is unusable. README was restored after an accidental reformat. 392 unit tests at 5.30ms/test, 49 integration at 214.96ms/test; sync, knowledge, secrets, reachability, hygiene and dogfood clean. checklists: passed. Uncommitted; next is ui verify --json and the React/Vite ui init pilot.

[milestone 3/3] Added ui verify --json with stable codes (ADR-167), the React/Vite ui init pilot (ADR-168), publish gate/test enforcement, contract validation, and plain-check auto-push blocking. 397 unit tests at 5.79ms/test, 49 integration at 206.76ms/test; sync, knowledge, secrets, reachability, hygiene and dogfood clean. checklists: passed. Remaining gaps: surface-changed-without-task evidence binding and optional rendered/a11y proof. Uncommitted.
Task 'ui-guard-enforcement-v1' completed successfully.

[1/4] Bind each declared UI surface to a finished task: record a surface digest in history and make strict check/publish refuse a surface whose current committed content has no matching finished UI task. [2/4] Return a JSON error envelope for ui verify --json, validate any present UI contract even when ui_required is false, and include those errors in the plain auto-push block. [3/4] Harden the React/Vite ui init pilot for peerDependencies and __tests__ protection, validate the generated contract, and print a gate summary before publish. [4/4] Correct the published ADR-165 integration-ceiling citation, record ADR-169, and run the full Phase 4 gate set.

impact_assessment.why: Probes confirmed that strict check passes a committed surface file with no UI task/history, ui verify --json emits human text on operational errors, and a malformed contract is ignored when ui_required is false; the pilot also has narrow detection and publish lacks a gate summary.
impact_assessment.benefits: A surface claim now requires matching evidence, CI receives JSON in all verify outcomes, malformed contracts fail even when the guard is not required, and the one-stack scaffold is safer.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: ui_history gains a surface_digest and strict/publish gain a surface-evidence refusal; dependency: none; concurrency: history writes remain under the task lock; state: history records without a digest cannot satisfy the new requirement until a new task finishes.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the evidence check opt-in through ui_required, record the digest at finish, add tests for matching and missing evidence, and document the migration behavior.

checkpoints.description: [milestone 4/4] Fixed the verified issues: surface digest evidence in ui_history with strict/publish enforcement, JSON ui.error envelopes, validation of any present contract, plain auto-push blocking, peerDependency and __tests__ support in ui init, generated-contract validation, publish gate summary, and the ADR-164/165 citation correction (ADR-169/170). 399 unit tests at 6.81ms/test, 49 integration at 220.45ms/test; sync, knowledge, secrets, reachability, hygiene and dogfood clean. checklists: passed. Uncommitted.
Task 'ui-guard-evidence-v1' completed successfully.

[1/1] Remove the evidence caveats: empty surfaces now require a finished-task digest, the digest includes permission bits, non-React/Vite projects can use ui init --fast/--paths, and legacy records get an explicit remedy. Verify the full gate set.

impact_assessment.why: The final review identified three security/coverage caveats in the UI evidence tranche: empty surfaces bypassed the gate, permission changes were invisible, and the scaffold was limited to React/Vite.
impact_assessment.benefits: A declared empty surface cannot bypass evidence, executable-bit changes alter the digest, and other stacks can create a manual zero-dependency contract without guessing a framework.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: ui_history records must now include a surface_digest for every surface, including empty ones; existing records without it require a new task; dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged; state: history schema gains a digest field.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the legacy remedy explicit, add tests for empty surfaces and the generic init override, include modes in the digest, and re-run every gate.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Caveat fixes verified: 402 unit tests at 5.62ms/test, 49 integration at 208.22ms/test; sync, knowledge, secrets, reachability and dogfood clean. Empty surfaces now need evidence, permission bits are in the digest, and generic ui init uses --fast/--paths. checklists: passed for AIKit; projects/tempo has an unrelated external hygiene finding. Uncommitted.
Task 'ui-guard-caveats-v1' completed successfully.

[1/6] Scaffold P1: make the ADR template non-parsing, strip HTML comments in the ADR audit, add bytecode/transient ignore rules, and fail cleanly when git identity is missing. [2/6] UI init P2: report when style lint is off, and derive generic protected patterns from the supplied surface paths instead of emitting dead src patterns. [3/6] Require a reason on ui allow, preserve reasons in history, and print them at finish. [4/6] Style lint: skip font properties whose value uses var(). [5/6] Hygiene: accept hygiene: allow on the finding line or the line immediately above it; warn on untracked README sources. [6/6] Update ADRs/docs/tests and run every Phase 4 gate; leave PRINCIPLE-015 R1 for explicit approval.

impact_assessment.why: The external report confirmed new-project blockers and UI guard accuracy defects: the commented ADR template poisons the register, Python bytecode dirties new projects, missing git identity is only a warning, style lint silently turns off, generic init emits dead patterns, allow has no reason, tokenized font declarations are flagged, and allow markers are too rigid.
impact_assessment.benefits: New projects can record their first ADR, run tests without dirtying the tree, and fail early on missing git identity; UI verification reports style coverage honestly; allow decisions are reviewable; and lint findings match the stated rules.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: allow gains a required --reason and task/history allowed_removals become objects; existing string entries remain readable; dependency: none; concurrency: task writes remain locked; state: ADR audit ignores HTML comments; git identity failure now rejects a half-made project.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep backward-compatible readers, add failing-first tests for each change, update ADR/docs, and run the full gate set.

checkpoints.description: [6/6] All six milestones implemented and verified. Phase 4 green on this exact tree: 409 unit (5.19ms/test) + 49 integration (216ms/test), sync --check, map --check, reachability, secrets --all, test budgets, dogfood 5/5. ADR-171 records all nine decisions; GUIDELINES.md P-011 R8 descriptive clause updated with the full 18-principle cross-check (0 Tier-1 files changed). Milestone 5's 'untracked README sources' decided as a named untracked-readme finding under the opt-in --artifacts mode (user did not recall the intent; rationale in ADR-171). checklists: passed, except PRINCIPLE-018 skipped (commit and push await user authorization per R1) and PRINCIPLE-019 staged-diff variant skipped in favour of the --all superset (nothing staged yet).
Task 'aikit-scaffold-lint-fixes-v1' completed successfully.

[1/4] Extract one readiness predicate so `status --exit-code` and the new JSON cannot disagree. [2/4] `status --json`: project metadata, the disruption audit, ui_task_open, gates, clean; ProjectError returns the stable error envelope. [3/4] `resume --json` over the same audit projection. [4/4] README, ADR, map and sync refresh, then every Phase 4 gate.

impact_assessment.why: CI and wrappers can read `aikit status <name>` only by parsing 15 lines of human prose; `--exit-code` already exists for the pass/fail bit, which proves the machine-readable need, and `ui verify --json` already establishes the envelope to copy. Nothing structured exists for `resume`, whose plan and next action are exactly what a cold-start wrapper needs.
impact_assessment.benefits: A documented JSON contract for the two orientation commands, built from the audit dict that already carries the data; one readiness predicate shared by the exit code and the payload, so the two delivery signals cannot drift apart the way ADR-155 and ADR-161 both had to repair.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: adds a second output surface for status and resume, and every JSON field becomes public under PRINCIPLE-004 R4; text output stays byte-identical so no existing reader breaks. dependency: none, json is stdlib and already imported. concurrency: read-only commands, no ledger or task writes. state: no schema or persisted file changes; the payload is computed per call from run_disruption_audit.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Reuse the ui verify envelope shape and its ProjectError handling rather than inventing one; compute the readiness bit once and feed both the exit code and the payload; add failing-first tests asserting the payload keys, the error envelope and that text mode is unchanged; document the fields in README within the 313-char headroom and record the contract in an ADR.

checkpoints.description: [4/4] All four milestones done. project_is_clean is the single readiness predicate behind --exit-code and the payload's clean key; status --json and resume --json print the Project Report Payload now documented in data_models.md; guidelines are carried as rules, not a count, so a JSON cold start cannot lose them (PRINCIPLE-004 R2); failures use one project.error envelope and keep 0/1/2. ADR-172 recorded. Phase 4 green: 461 tests, sync, map, reachability, secrets, budgets, dogfood 5/5. README at 22,390 of 22,500 chars (110 left). checklists: passed, except PRINCIPLE-018 push skipped (not authorized).
Task 'status-resume-json-v1' completed successfully.

[1/5] Widen SECRET_PATTERNS with prefixed high-confidence credential shapes and extend the private-key block to ENCRYPTED and SSH2 headers. [2/5] Add scrub_text(text) -> (scrubbed, detectors) using pattern detection only, never the entropy fallback, so prose keeps its hashes and digests. [3/5] disruption_recovery --checkpoint refuses credential-shaped free text and names --redact as the fix; --redact scrubs and writes. [4/5] subagent_delegate always scrubs the sub-agent's returned text and its JSON output. [5/5] README, data_models, ADR, map and sync refresh, then every Phase 4 gate.

impact_assessment.why: PRINCIPLE-019 R5 makes a leaked credential unrecoverable: it must be rotated, never reverted. The scanner already catches 15 shapes and already reads both ledgers and the dogfood log, but it only reports after the text is on disk, and the ledger's --why/--benefits/--risks/--mitigation fields are written straight into a git-tracked file. Blocking the write is worth more than reporting it afterwards, and the pattern table misses common prefixed formats (GitLab, npm, PyPI, SendGrid, HuggingFace, Telegram, Notion, Azure AccountKey and others).
impact_assessment.benefits: A credential quoted in an impact note is refused before it reaches a tracked file rather than found after; sub-agent output cannot carry a key into the lead agent's context or any downstream log; the pattern table roughly doubles while keeping the near-zero false-positive property the file's own design depends on.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --checkpoint gains a refusal path and a --redact flag, so a script writing credential-shaped free text now exits non-zero; existing checkpoint text is unaffected. dependency: none, re and the scanner are already imported where needed. concurrency: the refusal happens before the file lock is taken, so no partial write is possible. state: no schema change; scrubbing alters only the free-text field values that --redact is explicitly asked to rewrite.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add only prefixed shapes with literal anchors, never bare-length or PII patterns, and never apply the entropy fallback to prose, so legitimate commit hashes and digests in a risk note still pass; add a failing-first test per new pattern and per wiring point; make the refusal name --redact in its Fix line; scrub with a placeholder the STRONG_ALLOWLIST already recognizes so a scrubbed ledger stays clean on rescan.

checkpoints.description: [5/5] All five milestones done. SECRET_PATTERNS 15 -> 28 shapes, all vendor-prefixed; private-key block covers ENCRYPTED and SSH2. scrub_text runs patterns only, never the entropy fallback, so prose keeps hashes and digests (regression test). checkpoint_command refuses credential-shaped free text with exit 1 before reading or writing the ledger, --redact scrubs instead, on both CLI surfaces through the one ADR-128 path. answer_text scrubs sub-agent output unconditionally. ADR-173 recorded, data_models noted. Phase 4 green: 469 tests, all six gates, CLI contract, slowest --help 145ms of 200ms. README at 22,485 of 22,500 (15 left). checklists: passed, except PRINCIPLE-018 push skipped (not authorized).
Task 'secret-redaction-v1' completed successfully.
